title: Descent of transformations through fixed composite exact-functor realizations
statement:
Let $\mathcal M,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with their unbounded derived categories and quasi-isomorphism localizations $\mathsf L:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal M)\to D(\mathcal M)$ and $\mathsf L_B:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $G:\mathcal M\to\mathcal B$ and $H_r:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$ ($r\geq1$) be additive exact functors. Write $C$ for termwise application. Let $V:D(\mathcal M)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and $Q_r:D(\mathcal M)\to D(\mathcal M)$ be their exact induced functors with fixed canonical factorization isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]
$$v_K:V\mathsf L K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf L_B C(G)K,\qquad e_{r,K}:Q_r\mathsf L K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf L C(H_r)K.$$
For every natural transformation $\alpha:G\Rightarrow GH_r$, the degreewise maps $\alpha_{K^i}$ form a chain map $C(\alpha)_K:C(G)K\to C(G)C(H_r)K$, natural in every chain map $K\to K'$. Set $w_{r,K}=v_{C(H_r)K}\circ V(e_{r,K})$. There is a unique natural transformation $\alpha^D:V\Rightarrow VQ_r$ such that, for every complex $K$,
$$\alpha^D_{\mathsf L K}=w_{r,K}^{-1}\circ\mathsf L_B(C(\alpha)_K)\circ v_K.$$
Its naturality holds for every morphism in $D(\mathcal M)$, including inverses of localized quasi-isomorphisms. No invertibility of $\alpha$ is assumed.

Suppose also that $T_m:H_1H_m\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{m+1}$ and $t_m:Q_1Q_m\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{m+1}$ ($m\geq1$) are natural isomorphisms satisfying
$$e_{m+1,K}\circ t_{m,\mathsf L K}=\mathsf L(C(T_m)_K)\circ e_{1,C(H_m)K}\circ Q_1(e_{m,K}).$$
Then every well-typed equality of chain maps built from the $C(\alpha)$, $C(T_m)$, their functor images, identities and compositions remains an equality after localization and conjugation by the iterated specified factorizations, using the corresponding $\alpha^D$ and $t_m$. Equalities of natural transformations are detected on all objects $\mathsf L K$. If all $Q_r$ preserve a full subcategory $\mathcal C\subseteq D(\mathcal M)$, these transformations and equalities restrict to $\mathcal C$, with naturality for every morphism there.

proof.text: Naturality of $\alpha$ at $d_K^i$ gives $G(H_r(d_K^i))\alpha_{K^i}=\alpha_{K^{i+1}}G(d_K^i)$, exactly the chain-map condition. Naturality at each $f^i:K^i\to K^{\prime i}$ gives $C(G)C(H_r)(f)C(\alpha)_K=C(\alpha)_{K^{\prime}}C(G)(f)$. These component identities prove the asserted natural transformation on complexes. The same construction applies to $T_m$, its inverse, and transformations between any composites used below.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $\mathsf L$, the two functors $F_0,F_r$, their specified factors $v,w_r$, and $\mathsf L_B C(\alpha)$. It gives a unique natural transformation $\alpha^D:V\Rightarrow VQ_r$ with precisely the displayed component formula. In particular it is natural for every derived arrow. Explicitly, if $s:K\to K^{\prime}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, write $z=\mathsf L(s)$ and $b=\alpha^D$. Naturality $VQ_r(z)b_{\mathsf LK}=b_{\mathsf LK^{\prime}}V(z)$ implies $VQ_r(z)^{-1}b_{\mathsf LK^{\prime}}=b_{\mathsf LK}V(z)^{-1}$ by multiplying on the left and right by the two inverses. Only $z$ is inverted; $b$ need not be invertible.

proof.text: Use wordFactors and evaluationFactors as the recursively specified word comparison isomorphisms. Prove the square form of normalization: the derived expression followed by the target comparison equals the source comparison followed by the localized chain expression. The identity case uses preservation of identities; vertical composition follows by associativity, the two induction hypotheses, and preservation of composition. Cancel the final comparison isomorphism to obtain the stated conjugation formulas.

proof.text: For EndExpression.input, expand the product word comparison and use naturality of the derived transformation at the input word comparison, followed by the induction hypothesis on the input chain word. For EndExpression.output, apply the output derived functor to the induction hypothesis and use naturality of its word comparison at the chain-expression component. The compositor case is the supplied compatibility equation; for its inverse, postcompose with the localized forward compositor, use that equation, and cancel the two inverse pairs. Structural associators and unitors reduce to identities, with functoriality ensuring the recursively specified comparisons agree. For evaluation words, the product comparison is the input comparison mapped by the remaining derived word followed by V, then the evaluation comparison. This gives the same input-whiskering calculation. Sending an endomorphism pasting through G uses V applied to its normalized square and naturality of v.

proof.text: Induct on the finite expression for a well-typed chain-map composite: the generators have their conjugate formulas by Steps 3 and 4, including $T_m$ by Step 5; identities and vertical composition follow from cancellation in Step 4; each functor-image operation follows from the two whiskering calculations in Step 5. Thus each resulting derived expression, evaluated at $\mathsf LK$, is the localization of the original chain expression conjugated by its specified endpoint factors. Equal chain expressions therefore give equal components there. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] makes these equalities equalities of natural transformations on the whole derived category, and also gives the asserted general equality-detection property.

proof.text: Finally precompose $V$ and its transformations with the inclusion $\mathcal C\hookrightarrow D(\mathcal M)$. Each $Q_r$ restricts by hypothesis, as do its composites. Fullness means its component arrows, including the components of $t_m$ and their inverses, are arrows in $\mathcal C$ whenever their endpoints lie there. Naturality for any arrow of $\mathcal C$ is the already proved ambient naturality equation at that arrow. Precomposition preserves the equations just proved. This restriction does not require that a chosen representative $\mathsf LK$ itself belong to $\mathcal C$.
